plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding zero. Any bid above zero risks overpaying (winning with a small profit or losing with a cost). Since values are between $0 and $49, and we don't know the other bidders' values, bidding slightly above zero is the best we can do to potentially win without significant risk. My value is $3, so I'll bid a small amount to try and win.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, resulting in a loss when you would have profited. Bidding above your value risks overpaying. My value is $24, so I will bid $24.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, the expected value is $24.5. However, with only three bidders, the second highest bid will likely be lower. A conservative bid close to my value, but still aiming to win, is the best approach. I will bid $11.50.
